newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Leisurenet gets Planet Hollywood franchise.
newsitem.headline: Leisurenet gets Planet Hollywood franchise.

text.p: LeisureNet Ltd said at the weekend it had acquired the rights for Planet Hollywood International restaurants in South Africa through a franchise agreement and would open its first outlet in Cape Town later in 1997.

The company did not disclose the amount it had paid for the rights but said at the weekend that its restaurant division Foodgro planned to open further outlets in at least two other centres in the country.
Foodgro chief executive officer Christo Demetriades said they would pay five percent of an outlet's turnover in royalty fees.
"For the rights to the outlets Foodgro will pay a monthly royalty fee in rands... (of) five percent of the outlet's turnover," Demetriades said.
He said that the Cape Town outlet would cost an estimated 15-20 million rand to establish and would be launched in the fourth quarter of next year.

Based on international figures Demetriades said an average of 1,700-2,000 people a day were expected to visit the 500-seater restaurant. Turnover was expected to be 40 million rand per annum, he added.
Planet Holywood was the world's only dining experience inspired by the world of film and televion, he said.
Foodgro on Monday opened a merchandise store in Cape Town offering a full line of clothing and accessories as a forerunner to its first restaurant outlet.
